s1.syndrome_frame: Gradual-onset unilateral facial weakness with a mass in the ear canal
salient_findings: Nonpulsatile mass protruding through the inferior ear canal
Mild sensorineural hearing loss at 4000 Hz
key_facts: 2-year history of gradual-onset right facial weakness
Initially treated with oral steroids
No hearing loss, tinnitus, imbalance, or other cranial nerve deficits
Nonpulsatile mass in the inferior ear canal
Mild sensorineural hearing loss at 4000 Hz
MRI showed a 5 × 10-mm irregular lesion in the right mastoid
Lesion had heterogeneous enhancement on T1 with contrast
Expansion of the fallopian canal distal to the second genu of the facial nerve
Erosion of the posterior external auditory canal
Expansion of the stylomastoid foramen

shortlist.label: Facial nerve schwannoma
shortlist.why_kept: Gradual-onset unilateral facial weakness with a mass in the ear canal and imaging findings of a lesion in the right mastoid near the stylomastoid foramen

shortlist.label: Chondrosarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Imaging findings of a lesion with heterogeneous enhancement and expansion of the stylomastoid foramen, along with pathology showing cartilage and pleomorphic hyperchromatic nuclei

shortlist.label: Glomus jugulare tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of a nonpulsatile mass in the inferior ear canal and imaging findings of erosion of the posterior external auditory canal

shortlist.label: Facial nerve hemangioma
shortlist.why_kept: Imaging findings of a lesion in the right mastoid near the stylomastoid foramen and expansion of the fallopian canal distal to the second genu of the facial nerve

shortlist.label: Pleomorphic adenoma
shortlist.why_kept: Pathology showing pleomorphic hyperchromatic nuclei and a myxochondroid matrix, although less likely given the location and imaging findings

raw.rationale: The patient's 2-year history of gradual-onset right facial weakness, nonpulsatile mass in the inferior ear canal, and imaging findings of a lesion in the right mastoid with heterogeneous enhancement on T1 with contrast are consistent with a facial nerve schwannoma. The pathology results showing pleomorphic hyperchromatic nuclei, staining positive for S100, and low cellularity also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Chondrosarcoma
rejected.why: The pathology results do not support a diagnosis of chondrosarcoma, as the specimen consisted of cartilage but the microscopic examination showed pleomorphic hyperchromatic nuclei and staining positive for S100, which is more consistent with a schwannoma.

rejected.label: Glomus jugulare tumor
rejected.why: The patient's lack of hearing loss, tinnitus, and other cranial nerve deficits, as well as the imaging findings, do not support a diagnosis of glomus jugulare tumor, which typically presents with pulsatile tinnitus and hearing loss.

rejected.label: Facial nerve hemangioma
rejected.why: The imaging findings and pathology results do not support a diagnosis of facial nerve hemangioma, as there is no evidence of a vascular lesion.

rejected.label: Pleomorphic adenoma
rejected.why: The pathology results do not support a diagnosis of pleomorphic adenoma, as the specimen showed pleomorphic hyperchromatic nuclei and staining positive for S100, which is more consistent with a schwannoma.
